description: The Authority wishes to procure an economic operator to provide the following Internal Audit Services: The operation of the internal audit function should comply with the requirements outlined in the Code of Practice for the Governance of State Bodies. buyer: Newry, Mourne and Down District Council (NMD)
title: CA18575 - RFQ 2026/42 - Conservation Engineer for St Paul's Church The Crag Cemetery Rostrevor
description: Newry, Mourne & Down District Council looking for a Conservation Engineer who shall undertake a structural assessment of St Paul's Church and its environs and prepare a phased, costed conservation strategy addressing short-, medium- and long-term actions. St Paul's Church (ruins) is located within Crag Cemetery in the Rostrevor Conservation Area. The cemetery is accessed via a lane off Mary Street/The Square and is bounded by St Bronagh's GAA Clubrooms to the west, with residential development to the south and east. While the church is neither listed in its own right nor a scheduled monument, it is considered curtilage listed due to its proximity to a Grade B listed memorial (HB16/06/050). The church ruins are in a deteriorated and unstable condition, which has led to the closure of the graveyard on health and safety grounds. This has significant implications for public access, heritage value and community use. A structural appraisal was undertaken in 2019, with further recommendations issued in 2021. Although initial actions were progressed, the project subsequently stalled due to COVID-19 disruption and changes in personnel. The condition of the structure has since worsened, and the site remains closed. To access this competition: Registered: Login to https://suppliers.multiquote.com and view the opportunity CA18575. Not registered: Visit https://suppliers.multiquote.com then register and quote CA18575 as the reason for registration. Any queries please contact MultiQuote on 020 3920 8054.

description: Hankinnan kohteena on ratkaisu, jonka avulla voidaan tarjota tietoturvallisesti eristetty ja hallittu palvelinsäilö varmuuskopioidulle datalle. Ratkaisun tulee mahdollistaa varmuuskopioiden turvallinen säilytys, käsittely ja hyödyntäminen erillisessä, tuotantoympäristöstä irrotetussa kokonaisuudessa. TIETOJENKÄSITTELYN OIKEUTUS, SIJAINTI, HALLINTAYHTEYDET JA SUOJAUS Hankinnan kohteena oleva palvelimen turvasäilö -palvelu sisältää Tilaajan varmistusympäristöstä replikoitavaa varmistusdataa, joka voi sisältää Tilaajan oman datan ohella myös mm. omistaja-asiakkaiden potilastietojärjestelmien tietoja ja siten EU:n yleisen tietosuoja-asetuksen 9 artiklassa tarkoitettuja erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvia henkilötietoja. Erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvien tietojen käsittely on lähtökohtaisesti kiellettyä, mutta käsittely on sallittua, kun kieltoon on säädetty poikkeus. Tässä palvelussa käsittely on välttämätöntä terveydenhuollon tietojärjestelmien ja palvelujen hallinnoimiseksi sekä palvelujen jatkuvuuden ja palautettavuuden varmistamiseksi (GDPR 9(2)(h)). Käsittely toteutetaan omistaja-asiakkaiden (rekisterinpitäjien) ohjeiden mukaisesti; Tilaaja toimii henkilötietojen käsittelijänä ja vastaa alikäsittelijöiden (Toimittaja mahdollisine alihankkijoineen) hallinnasta. Rekisterinpitäjien osoitusvelvollisuuden, valvottavuuden ja käsiteltävien tietojen korkean suojaustason varmistamiseksi Tilaaja edellyttää, että: 1) varmistusdata säilytetään ja sitä käsitellään yksinomaan Suomen alueella sijaitsevissa konesaleissa, ja 2) myös palvelun hallintayhteydet (ylläpito- ja hallintaliikenne sekä mahdolliset etähallintaratkaisut) ovat sallittuja vain Suomen alueelta, ja 3) varmistusdata on salattuna (siirrossa ja levossa) ja palvelu tuotetaan ainoastaan Tilaajalle dedikoidussa ympäristössä. Vaatimus on rajattu koskemaan vain hankinnan kohteena olevaa varmistuspalvelua ja on oikeassa suhteessa hankinnan tavoitteeseen ja käsiteltävien tietojen luonteeseen nähden. OPTIO Optiona pyydetään hinnoittelua analytiikkapalvelulle (Eristetty analytiikkaympäristö ransomware- ja virusskannauksineen), joka toimii täysin erillisessä verkkovyöhykkeessä ilman pääsyä tuotantoverkkoon. Kyseistä palvelua voidaan hankkia sopimusaikana tarpeen mukaan, minkä vuoksi se on vertailuhinnassa mukana vain yhden vuoden osalta.

The conditions report shall be prepared after a thorough investigation of the existing conditions with estimated costs and improvements. The following design will include all selected repairs and improvements from the conditions report that fit within VA construction budget. As part of the report and design effort, the existing conditions shall be tested and verified, including evaluation of the drainage, materiality, masonry, fall protection, equipment, ACM, insulation, and structural integrity. title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – BIM-Planungsleistung - ZKB 2030 - Friedrichshafen Flughafen und Meckenbeuren
description: Gegenstand der Vergabe sind BIM-Planungsleistungen (Einfach BIM) für die Erneuerung der Verkehrsstationen Friedrichshafen Flughafen und Meckenbeuren an der Strecke 4500. Die Planung erfolgt als Einphasenplanung für die Leistungsphasen 1 bis 7 gemäß HOAI unter Anwendung der BIM-Methodik. An beiden Haltepunkten sind jeweils die zwei vorhandenen Bahnsteige zu erneuern. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst insbesondere die Erneuerung der Bahnsteigbeläge, die Erneuerung der Bahnsteigkanten, die Erneuerung der Beleuchtungsanlagen sowie den Austausch der Ausstattungselemente. Am Haltepunkt Meckenbeuren ist zusätzlich die Erneuerung des Stufenbelags der Personenunterführung vorgesehen. Projektstandorte: Friedrichshafen Flughafen (Bahnhofs-Nr. 5987) Strecke 4500, km 193,0 bis km 193,3 Meckenbeuren (Bahnhofs-Nr. 4015) Strecke 4500, km 188,7 bis km 189,0 Ziel des Projekts ist die Modernisierung der Bahnsteiganlagen zur Verbesserung der Verkehrssicherheit, Funktionalität und Aufenthaltsqualität unter Anwendung der BIM-Methodik. Folgende Leistungsbilder sind Bestandteil der Vergabe: - Objektplanung Verkehrsanlagen gemäß HOAI - Fachplanung 50-Hz-Anlagen einschließlich Bahnsteigbeleuchtung - Objekt- und Tragwerksplanung Ingenieurbauwerke für die Erneuerung der Treppenanlagen bzw. Treppenbeläge - Baugrunduntersuchungen einschließlich Baugrundgutachten - Erstellung eines BIM-Grundlagenmodells auf Basis der bereitgestellten Vermessungsdaten Die Planung ist unter Berücksichtigung der bahnbetrieblichen Randbedingungen, der Anforderungen an die Barrierefreiheit sowie der gültigen Regelwerke der DB InfraGO AG durchzuführen.

title: Tobyhanna Gates & Turnstiles
description: SEE PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT FOR DETAILS PART 1 � GENERAL INFORMATION 1. General This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees. 1.1 Description of Services/Introduction This is a non-personal service(s) contract to provide Gates, Barriers, and Turnstiles Service and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform service and maintenance on vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles at Tobyhanna Army Depot as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. 1.2 Background Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) relies on a comprehensive physical security infrastructure to protect personnel, equipment, and mission-critical assets. The vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles are essential components of this infrastructure. Consistent preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and targeted technical upgrades are required to ensure continuous operational readiness and compliance with DoD physical security standards. 1.3 Scope The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in this PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents. 1.4 Objectives Ensure all gates, barriers, and turnstiles are adequately maintained to prevent failures and extend equipment lifecycle. Return damaged or degraded devices to full service quickly through a 24/7 emergency response capability. Maintain reliable function when activated to secure Tobyhanna Army Depot perimeters. Complete initial technical baseline repairs and upgrades safely and efficiently.

title: RFI Comprehensive Medical Review & Audit Support
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with FAR Part 10 to conduct market research. The Government's purpose is planning only; this notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP)/Request for Quotation (RFQ) nor a promise to issue one in the future. The Government will not pay any costs for responding, and any submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurement. The Government is not seeking proposals or quotes at this time. Scope of Interest / Functional Areas: The Government is assessing the market�s capability to provide comprehensive support under the following disciplines: a. Audits for Medicare Parts A, B, D, and Medicaid medical record review and consultative services b. Audits for Medicare Part C medical record review and consultative services c. Evaluations and Inspections medical record review and consultative services d. Expert consultant and witness services in support of the Office of Investigations and/or Office of Counsel to the Inspector General A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is provided for industry feedback; requirements may change prior to any future solicitation. Requested Information (do not submit proposals or quotes): Please provide high level, non price specific information addressing the elements below. Do not include proprietary pricing, line item estimates, or any proposal/quote content. Section 1: Corporate Capability & Experience a. PWS Alignment: Demonstrate your organization's core capability to fulfill the functional areas outlined in the draft PWS. b. Medical Review Experience: Outline your firm's high-level experience in conducting large-volume medical claims reviews for audits and evaluations and inspections; and support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses specifically across the following five domains (as referenced in the attached PWS): 1. Audit Medicare Parts A/B/D and Medicaid 2. Audit Medicare Part C 3. Evaluations and Inspections 4. Office of Investigations 5. Office of Counsel to the Inspector General c. Geographic Reach: Describe your prior experience managing and executing nationwide or multi-jurisdictional medical claim reviews. d. Capacity & Scalability: State your organization's maximum monthly claim review capacity, including your approach to scaling operations between normal workloads and surge conditions. e Teaming & Subcontracting: Identify potential subcontracting partners or specialized vendors you would anticipate utilizing, including an estimated percentage breakdown of work performed by the prime contractor versus subcontractors. Section 2: High-Level Technical Approach & Operations a. High-Level Technical Methodology: Describe your conceptual approach to fulfilling the core tasks in PWS. Please limit this narrative to no more than 5 pages total, organized by the 5 PWS sections. Focus on your overarching claims review methodology, general sampling plan frameworks, documentation standards, and typical project timelines rather than a granular, step-by-step solution. b. Quality & Accuracy Frameworks: Outline your corporate quality assurance processes, internal review protocols, and standard strategies used to reduce error rates and ensure consistency across large volumes. b. Staffing & Key Qualifications: Provide a conceptual staffing structure or organizational chart. Identify the typical roles, credentials (e.g., MD, RN, CPC), and qualifications of the key personnel required to successfully support a PWS of this nature. Please identify whether these staff will need to be hired or if they are current employees/contractors. Also, indicate staffing availability for physicians with specialties (i.e. hospice, vascular surgeon, nephrologist, physical medicine and rehabilitation or physiatrists). c. Risk & Mitigation: Identify the primary technical or operational challenges anticipated with a medical review scope of this size and outline your high-level mitigation strategies. Section 3: Past Performance & Market Pricing a. Relevant Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of similar Federal medical review contracts performed within the last five years. Also, provide up to three examples of similar Federal support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses within the last five years. b. Performance Outcomes: Summarize the high-level outcomes of those past contracts, focusing on standard metrics such as timeliness, accuracy rates (including rate at which findings were overturned during the appeals process), and a history of successful audit findings. c. Cost Drivers & Efficiencies: Provide a general overview of your commercial pricing structure and the primary cost drivers (e.g., specific labor categories, specialized technology/AI tools, administrative overhead). Highlight any built-in efficiencies or innovative workflows in your approach that typically yield cost savings for the government. Section 4: Industry Feedback & PWS Refinement a. Clarity & Feasibility Review: Identify any requirements, metrics, or tasks within the draft PWS that appear ambiguous, overly restrictive, or technologically infeasible based on current commercial market capabilities. b. Recommendations for Improvement: Suggest specific enhancements, industry standard metrics, or structural changes to the PWS that would improve the clarity, feasibility, and competitiveness of the final solicitation. Submission Instructions: Email responses by November 13, 2026, 12:00 PM Eastern Time to the Points of Contact below. Mark proprietary information clearly; the Government may use non proprietary information to refine its acquisition approach. Points of Contact: a. Contracting Officer: Shavonda Jamison � Shavonda_Jamison@ibc.doi.gov b. Contracting Specialist: Dorothy Royster � Dorothy_Royster@ibc.doi.gov Attachments: a. Draft PWS (for market research and feedback only; subject to change). Disclaimer: This RFI is for market research; it does not commit the Government to any acquisition. The Government will not reimburse costs for responding. Not responding does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. No proposals or quotes will be accepted in response to this notice.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial construction for MDC Brooklyn located at 80 29th Street Brooklyn, NY, 11232, and is prepared in accordance with the format in subpart FAR Revision Subpart 12.202(b)(1), as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. MDC Brooklyn is a federal correctional facility located at 80 29th Street Brooklyn, NY 11232. The contractor is responsible to provide all equipment and labor to remove and replace all existing shower partitions (with attached changing rooms) and bathroom stall partitions on the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, and 6th floors of the East Building at MDC Brooklyn. title: Tobyhanna Gates & Turnstiles
description: SEE PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT FOR DETAILS NOTE: The Addendum cites solicitation W51AA1-26-Q-A100 instead of W51AA1-27-Q-A010 twice. Ignore this, it will be corrected with the first amendment. PART 1 � GENERAL INFORMATION 1. General This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees. 1.1 Description of Services/Introduction This is a non-personal service(s) contract to provide Gates, Barriers, and Turnstiles Service and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform service and maintenance on vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles at Tobyhanna Army Depot as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. 1.2 Background Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) relies on a comprehensive physical security infrastructure to protect personnel, equipment, and mission-critical assets. The vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles are essential components of this infrastructure. Consistent preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and targeted technical upgrades are required to ensure continuous operational readiness and compliance with DoD physical security standards. 1.3 Scope The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in this PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents. 1.4 Objectives Ensure all gates, barriers, and turnstiles are adequately maintained to prevent failures and extend equipment lifecycle. Return damaged or degraded devices to full service quickly through a 24/7 emergency response capability. Maintain reliable function when activated to secure Tobyhanna Army Depot perimeters. Complete initial technical baseline repairs and upgrades safely and efficiently.

title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: 23 October 2026: P00001 Extend the due date to 13 November 2026. **Please take note that the solicitation number has been updated to HTC71127QE127 due to overlap in Fiscal Years** The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

title: Cost Per Reportable Result Purchase of Immunohistochemistry Reagents for Laboratory Tests.
description: The VA Puget Sound Health Care System Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Service requires a histology staining workflow system which includes: Two (2) immunohistochemistry (IHC) and two (2) in-situ hybridization (ISH) immunostainers, and two (2) special stainers, and a specimen tracking system which promotes proper identification of specimens and slides and will audit workflow to identify areas that need improvement and reduce errors. The tracking system will improve patient safety, provide a chain of custody, and will monitor productivity. All the components of the workflow system must communicate with each other in order to track the workflow. The stainers attached to this system must be automated and allow the system to track and label slides for special staining and immunostaining. The workflow system must be compatible with the IT systems VISTA and/or Cerner, as well as any other new electronic health record system the VA acquires and also be compatible with Data Innovations middleware.

title: Quality Assurance Services - Civil Works, Interagency and International Services (IIS), and Military Construction Projects in Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District issues this Request for Proposals (RFP) to award an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Quality Assurance Services across Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. This procurement follows the presolicitation notice previously synopsized under solicitation number W51DQV26RA007. The contractor shall provide comprehensive quality assurance oversight supporting Civil Works, International and Interagency Services (IIS), and Military Construction (MILCON) projects, including navigation, flood risk management, coastal protection, environmental restoration, water resources, and military or federal installations. Services encompass monitoring contractor compliance with plans and specifications, reviewing engineering submittals and technical reports, conducting on-site field inspections of dams, levees, berms, cutoff walls, pump stations, flood control gates, and electrical systems, and performing certified sampling and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, and water. Contract personnel shall also perform daily safety monitoring and prepare daily quality assurance inspection reports. This action is a total small business set-aside under NAICS code 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) with an applicable small business size standard of $19.5 million. The contract ordering period comprises a one-year base period, four 12-month option periods, and one six-month option period, not to exceed a total duration of five years and six months, with a maximum program capacity of $35 million across the contract life.

title: E-Waste Collection Events
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance LLC (BEA), the Management and Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified recyclers capable of organizing residential electronic waste (e-waste) collection events in states without e-waste recycling regulation (i.e., nonregulated states) to support INL�s research and operational mission. This service is essential for raising awareness, increasing collection volumes and verifying whether successful collection methods from a regulated state can be applied to a nonregulated state with comparable results. Eligible states for this work include Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Idaho (except eastern and southeastern region), Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota, Tennessee and Wyoming. BACKGROUND BEA is the Management and Operating Contractor for the DOE located at INL. INL is a DOE national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security and advanced energy innovation. A BEA research team has the lead role on the DOE project titled, �Comparing Strategies to Collect Battery-Containing Devices in States with and without Electronics Recycling Laws.� The proposed service will operate to support this project through Sept. 30, 2027. In the first two years of this project, project teams organized collection events in New York and Idaho. New York is as urban area with established e-waste regulations, and Idaho is a rural area without such requirements. By applying successful collection methods from New York to southeastern Idaho, we observed similar success across 20 e-waste collection events. To further validate these results, we are seeking opportunities to apply our methods in other nonregulated states by organizing six to nine e-waste collection events. SCOPE OF WORK Responding organizations must be capable of delivering the following services: Provide existing status; compile data from existing residential collection activities related to seasonal trends, locations and e-waste types. Organize collection events at new locations in nonregulated states, with each participating organization conducting at least two to three collection events before September 2027. Arrange advertisements on multiple channels to broadcast new collection events and raise awareness about battery-containing e-waste recycling. Provide collection event data including number of participants and quantities of collected e-waste by type PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors should submit an EOI that includes the following: Organization information: Organization name, address, organization type, scope of operations, number of employees and primary point of contact. Existing e-waste collection access: Describe existing e-waste collection events, permanent drop-off locations or other collection options available in the proposed service area. Program interest and expected outcomes: Explain why your organization wants to participate in this project and what outcomes you expect to achieve. Service area and target participants: Identify the cities, counties, or communities that will be served by the proposed e-waste collection activities. Community need: Describe the primary e-waste management challenges or unmet needs in the proposed service area. Collection plan: Describe the proposed e-waste collection activities for the program year (by Sept. 1, 2027). Provide the anticipated number of collection events and proposed cities, counties, or collection locations. Provide communication strategies (i.e. social media, mail, news, flyers, etc.) to raise awareness and promote collection events. Downstream e-waste management: Identify who will transport, receive, recycle, process, or otherwise manage the collected e-waste. Recycler/processor qualifications: Identify relevant certifications or qualifications of the entities handling collected e-waste, such as R2, e-Stewards, or other applicable certifications. Partnership with local nonprofit organizations or local authorities: Specify whether the proposed e-waste collection activities involve collaboration with local nonprofit organizations or governmental authorities. Deadline for submission: Nov. 13, 2026 (date subject to change) Submit to: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov Technical Point of Contact: ThiThuyTien.Le@inl.gov Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated Request for Proposal solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

title: USCG Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. title: Vacuum Turbo Pumps
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing Turbomolecular Pumping Stations. The Turbomolecular Pumping Station (TMPS) will replace the Agilent Technologies/Varian TPS-compact TV301 (Model: 969-8221M003), which contains the following components: TV301 turbomolecular pump, integrated controller, variable leak valve and dry scroll backing pump. The manufacturer (Agilent/Varian) has discontinued this item and ceased its support of the key components. This acquisition will aid AFMETCAL in maintaining support for a multitude of different high-vacuum and vacuum metrology calibration equipment across the Air Force. The new standard would support high-vacuum chambers, vacuum sensors, transducers, and other similar high-vacuum TMDE. The TMPS shall evacuate vacuum TMDE up to high-vacuum levels in absolute mode. Responses will assist AFMETCAL in determining the availability of qualified sources and the appropriate acquisition strategy. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity of 86 units over 5 years. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. (4) advise if you have the item on a GSA schedule or other Government contract include front page of schedule and the page showing the part is on award (5) provide information concerning the technical capabilities of the product you are interested in offering, including commercial literature/brochures and warranty. Describe any awards you have been involved in that are the same as or similar to what is described in this RFI. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. Ensure only .pdf, .doc or .xls documents are attached to your email. Submit all responses to the listed point of contact. If an email response is not possible, submit by FAX to 937-713-5841 or mail to 813 Irving-wick Dr W., Horton Building, Heath OH 43056-1199. Reference 27M-083A-VA in all correspondence. Responses are due by 11/13/2026 at 2:00pm ET or 1400 hours; however, early responses are encouraged. Point of Contact - Frank Capuano, Contract Specialist, Phone 937-713-5842 Email:frank.capuano@us.af.mil.

title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

title: Request For Information (570628) Ready Building - Industry Feedback
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought Notice/RFI � Ready Building, Fort Bliss, Texas DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP) or an Invitation for Bids (IFB). This notice is issued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Construction and Repair) and is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). No solicitation is available at this time. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding Design-Build to Budget (DBtB), project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support the upcoming project delivery selection. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The planned procurement will construct a Ready Building, Project Number 570628, at Biggs Army Airfield, Fort Bliss, El Paso, Texas. The project will provide a permanent, properly sized Ready Building supporting continuous, 24-hour operations for an on-call Air MEDEVAC crew. The facility will provide approximately 4,836 square feet of permanent single-story construction. The facility will provide operational space for a five-person aircraft crew, living and readiness space for one five-person crew, and surge capacity for an additional five-person crew. The facility must enable aircraft crews to remain postured for rapid response, with direct access to the aircraft parking apron for MEDEVAC launches and weekend aircraft maintenance. The existing temporary facility is undersized and is not adjacent to the aircraft parking apron. The existing facility will remain operational until construction of the new Ready Building is complete. The temporary facility is outside the new construction footprint and is included in the project demolition scope after completion of the new facility. The project site is adjacent to the Biggs Army Airfield aircraft parking apron. The project site is anticipated to fall within a seismic design condition that may result in Seismic Design Category D requirements. The final Seismic Design Category will be determined by the project Designer of Record in accordance with applicable codes and project-specific site conditions. The Ready Building is a Risk Category IV facility because of its emergency-response function. The project must comply with applicable Unified Facilities Criteria, antiterrorism/force-protection, fire/life-safety, seismic, cybersecurity, and installation requirements. Fort Bliss utility systems are privatized. Required services include electric power, natural gas or an approved alternative fuel approach, water, sanitary sewer, and telecommunications. Utility-system owners are anticipated to provide and own required connections to the facility service disconnect or other defined point of demarcation. The civil utility plan identifies a need for utility-owner rerouting of water and gas around the proposed lid pond. title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

title: Request for Information for U-2 Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System -2
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the repair data, expertise, capabilities, manufacturing, engineering, software development, maintenance and experience to meet qualification requirements to repair and sustain the Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System (ASARS)-2 components and ground support equipment. The level of security clearance and amount of overseas continental united states participation in this requirement has not been determined. The Government does not own or have access to the data for ASARS-2 sensor. The Government has determined that this system is a noncommercial item. Contractor shall furnish all material, support equipment, tools, test equipment, and services. The contractor is responsible for providing, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at their facility or a subcontractor�s facility. Contractor furnished material or parts used for replacement shall equal or exceed the quality of the original material or parts. Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. The government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey. The Air Force requires long-term support and sustainment of the Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System (ASARS) -2, which provides near-real-time high-resolution, long-range imagery from ground returns during day or night, in all weather conditions. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. This effort requires cybersecurity support and sustainment in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 503, and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) process, Cybersecurity Impact Evaluation Recommendation (CIER) for all changes and modifications of this effort to incorporate in the U-2S Approval to Operate (ATO) package, Cybersecurity Authorization Package (CAP), Risk Management Framework (RMF), Interim Authority to Test (IATT), Interim Authority to Connect (ATC), and/or separate ATO, as applicable and requested by the Government. This effort also requires Depot Maintenance Support Teams (DMST) to support the following sustainment activities: mission software updates; Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) engineering; engineering change proposals; configuration management (hardware and software); integration with ASARS-related systems on the U-2 platform; data management; technical data (such as technical manuals and reports) development and maintenance; in-plant Specialized Repair Activity and sparing; technical and engineering actions for calibrating ASARS-2; resolving system failures/issues in a timely manner; and planning/preparation/implementation of system sustainment improvements.

description: Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day Important Dates: Industry Day Registration Deadline -- 3:00 PM EDT on Friday, November 13, 2026 Industry Day -- 9:00 AM EDT on Tuesday, November 17, 2026 1. Introduction For over 10 years, TSA has held regular events to engage with external aviation security stakeholders, including airports, airport designers, airlines, equipment vendors, industry groups, and other domestic and international industry stakeholders in support of TSA�s mission. TSA has capitalized on these events to: Promote TSA�s checkpoint system of systems designs and standards; Encourage collaboration within the aviation security community; Share best practices from a variety of operating environments, facility sizes, and capabilities; Learn about the latest security technology advances and industry innovations; and Engage with stakeholders early in the design process to allow TSA to influence designs and support public-private partnerships. 2. title: Italy – Refuse disposal and treatment – Procedura aperta, ai sensi dell'art. 71, d.lgs. 36/2023, articolata in n. 4 lotti, per l'affidamento del Servizio di raccolta, trasporto, smaltimento e/o recupero dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti e luoghi di produzione della RAI S.p.A. di Roma, Torino, Milano e Napoli
description: L’appalto ha ad oggetto il servizio di raccolta, trasporto, smaltimento e/o trattamento/recupero dei rifiuti speciali (pericolosi e non pericolosi), prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai, comprensivi dei relativi cantieri e set esterni, localizzati nelle città di Roma, Torino, Milano e Napoli e relative zone limitrofe il cui elenco è dettagliato nel progetto di servizi. Saltuariamente l’attività di raccolta, trasporto, smaltimento e/o trattamento/recupero dei rifiuti, potrà avvenire su tutto il territorio italiano per quanto concerne i cantieri e set esterni (come, ad esempio, per la manifestazione del Festival di Sanremo). Il servizio si articola nelle seguenti fasi: a) supporto; b) analisi di caratterizzazione del rifiuto; c) movimentazione interna; d) raccolta; e) pulizia delle aree; f) trasporto; g) conferimento; h) intermediazione; i) smaltimento; j) recupero. Rientra nell’appalto, altresì, la fornitura di contenitori vuoti e di contenitori aggiuntivi nonché l’etichettatura e la cartellonistica. Al fine di garantire il contemperamento tra la necessità di i) favorire la massima partecipazione e l’accesso delle MPMI, nonché, comunque, ii) razionalizzare la spesa ed efficientare il processo d’acquisto, ai sensi di quanto previsto dall’articolo 58, comma 4, d.lgs. 36/2023, ciascun concorrente – pur potendo presentare offerta per tutti i lotti in cui è articolata la gara - non potrà aggiudicarsi più di un lotto; la relativa aggiudicazione avverrà seguendo l’ordine decrescente dell’importo economico dei lotti, partendo dal valore più alto. Qualora non fosse possibile procedere all’aggiudicazione di uno o più lotti per mancanza di offerte ad esito di quanto sopra previsto, la stazione appaltante, al fine di assicurare il soddisfacimento del fabbisogno, si riserva la facoltà di aggiudicare gli eventuali lotti residui anche in deroga al suddetto limite di aggiudicazione, laddove risultassero offerte valide presentate da concorrenti già aggiudicatari di un lotto, purché in possesso dei relativi requisiti. In particolare, il servizio ha ad oggetto la trattazione delle seguenti tipologie di Codici EER: - Codici passivi, per i quali il fornitore riceverà un importo per la quantità (Kg, Litri o Metri cubi, ovvero numero di ritiri nel caso dei rifiuti ambulatoriali e sanitari) di rifiuto effettivamente trasportato e conferito a destinazione finale. L’importo unitario per ciascun codice è da intendersi comprensivo anche delle spese di carico, trasporto e conferimento; - Codici a titolo gratuito, per i quali il servizio sarà svolto dall’aggiudicatario senza il pagamento di un corrispettivo; - Codici attivi, per i quali l’appaltatore corrisponderà alla RAI il corrispettivo indicato in sede di offerta e valido per l’intera durata del Contratto. Per la dettagliata descrizione delle caratteristiche tecniche e funzionali del Servizio nonché delle modalità di esecuzione dello stesso e del dettaglio delle sedi di intervento si rimanda al Progetto di Servizi. Ai sensi dell’art. 58 del Codice, l’appalto è suddiviso nei seguenti n. 4 lotti: o Lotto n. 1: Servizio di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai di Roma; o Lotto n. 2: Servizio di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai di Torino; o Lotto n. 3: Servizio di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai di Milano; o Lotto n. 4: Servizio di smaltimento dei rifiuti speciali prodotti presso gli insediamenti Rai di Napoli. Tenuto conto dei principi in materia, il perimetro di ciascun lotto è stato definito applicando un criterio geografico per un bilanciamento tra obiettivi diversi: mantenere una logica di continuità territoriale per la preminente esigenza connessa ad un efficiente gestione della prestazione contrattuale e, al contempo, consentire la partecipazione alle microimprese, piccole e medie imprese (MPMI) in grado di modulare la propria offerta in relazione a potenziali specificità territoriali. Non si è ritenuto di procedere ad un’ulteriore frammentazione delle prestazioni all’interno dei singoli ambiti territoriali, in quanto le attività oggetto di affidamento presentano una forte integrazione operativa, gestionale ed amministrativa e richiedono un coordinamento unitario nell’ambito del medesimo insediamento. Un’ulteriore suddivisione avrebbe potuto determinare inefficienze gestionali, sovrapposizioni organizzative e maggiori oneri di coordinamento contrattuale, senza apportare significativi benefici in termini di apertura del mercato.

title: Request for White Papers: Intelligence Resource Execution and Oversight (Project Argus)
description: Intelligence Resource Execution and Oversight (Project Argus)- HQ0034279R001 Area of Interest: The Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (USW(I&S)) requires a prototype solution to replace the legacy Budget and Intelligence Related Database (BIRD). USW(I&S) is responsible for overseeing intelligence resource execution across the Department. The current BIRD system, developed and maintained by multiple contractor teams over more than a decade using disparate technology stacks and evolving priorities, now suffers from outdated software frameworks, inefficient code, and an overly complex database schema. These deficiencies impede timely analysis, increase manual workload, and limit the ability of analysts to support senior leader decision-making on intelligence resources. USW(I&S) seeks a modern, flexible, and extensible system that enables efficient ingestion, cataloguing, analysis, and visualization of intelligence resource data. The desired end-state is a single, user-friendly platform that supports rapid querying, analytic dashboards, and an intuitive interface (including special intelligence-enabled natural language queries) so that analysts can produce accurate, timely insights and the Congressional Justification Book (CJB) with significantly reduced manual effort. The prototype solution must deliver the following core capabilities (additional modules may be required based on evolving USW(I&S) priorities): Ingestion and management of current and historical Intelligence Resource data and execution data. Data will be uploaded by multiple users spanning the Department of War, i.e. Agencies and Services. Access to and ability to upload shall be controlled by the Office of the USW(I&S). Financial management query tool and data analytics supported by Super Intelligence so users can interact with the database for in-depth analysis. This tool should have the ability to create data visualizations. User defined Visual Dashboard creation capability that utilizes resource data uploaded into the system database. Congressional Justification Book (CJB) Generator capable of combining quantitative data and narrative inputs from both internal and external stakeholders to produce the CJB. This tool shall take input from users spanning the Department of War, i.e. Agencies and Services. Access to and ability to input shall be controlled by the Office of the USW(I&S). System should operate at multiple classification levels, i.e. development at an UNCLASSIFIED level that is transferable to the SECRET and TOP SECRET networks; data held at a lower level should be replicated to the higher level. Specific Modules: CJB Execution Countries of Interest tracking Congressional Marks tracking Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDC) data management The system must be able to ingest data from common formats (including Microsoft PowerPoint, PDF, and Excel). Offerors may propose either cloud-based or on-premise solutions (or a hybrid approach). Any proposal must include a clear comparison of the pros and cons of the proposed hosting approach, including considerations of cost, security, performance, scalability, and transportability. The solution must support development in an unclassified environment while remaining transportable and operable across Impact Levels (IL) 2 through 7. USW(I&S) requires direct, on-site engagement between the development team and government analysts throughout the prototype effort to ensure the solution meets operational needs. In the event that the proposed system is not ready for deployment by September 2027, respondents must address their ability to sustain the legacy BIRD system on-site within its classified environment while finalizing the new system. Additionally, respondents must outline their approach to providing the required minimum of 12 months of on-site sustainment following successful transition to ensure full system operability and rapid response. Special Considerations: Place of Performance: For development, the primary places of performance will be the Pentagon and a contractor-provided development site. If required to sustain BIRD, the primary place of performance will be the Pentagon. Travel and Remote Work: Alternate work locations are authorized for development activities. Direct, on-site engagement between the development team and government analysts is required throughout the prototype effort to ensure the solution meets operational needs. Situational telework may be approved on a case-by-case basis. CONUS travel is authorized as mission needs require and is subject to Government approval. Security: Top Secret / Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) facility clearance and personnel clearances are required. Personnel supporting classified development, sustainment, or analytic functions shall possess the appropriate clearance level for their role, up to and including Top Secret / SCI. Cybersecurity, Information Assurance, and Regulatory Compliance: The solution must comply with all applicable Department of War and Intelligence Community cybersecurity, information assurance, and related requirements. This includes, but is not limited to, the Risk Management Framework (RMF); National Institute of Standards and Technology; Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM); Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs); software version update strategies to remain compliant with DISA Standard Parts List (SPL); and relevant DoD Instructions (including DoDI 8500.01 and DoDI 8510.01). The performer shall support the Government in obtaining and maintaining the necessary Authorizations to Operate (ATO) across Impact Levels (IL) 2 through 7. Please see the attachment for more information and the white paper template. Please submit your company's white paper to Ms. Ashley Brink (ashley.a.brink.civ@mail.mil) and Ms. Carrie Martin (carrie.e.martin13.civ@mail.mil) NLT 05:00pm EST on November 13, 2026.

title: Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS) Production
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT SEEKING OR ACCEPTING UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS. This notice is a Request for Information (RFI) as defined in FAR 15.101(c). The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) is conducting market research for the Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS). ACNS helps to determine vessel position based on optical sighting of celestial objects including stars and resident space objects (RSOs) such as satellites and space debris. Ship�s position derived from ACNS shall be used to improve the resilience of the surface ship Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) system of systems suite by providing an Alternative Position Source (APS) to support Assured PNT. U.S. Navy and commercial enterprises leverage a variety of navigation solutions that allow vessels to safely navigate with and without GPS. The U.S. Navy is looking to modernize legacy systems over time. This RFI seeks information on prospective technologies that could be leveraged or developed as enablers for an ACNS solution. This RFI seeks to understand how interested parties would integrate the ACNS with navigation sensors and other ship equipment specifically Global Positioning System-Based Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Service (GPNTS). PAE MS invites all interested potential sources, including small business concerns, to submit written information sufficient to demonstrate the respondent�s ability to fulfill the requirements. For those interested parties that have technologies which may not achieve a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 8-9 by FY 2029, please provide information on current research and development efforts that may address some or all requirements of this RFI beyond FY 2029. Responses are requested by 13 November 2026. Questions or clarifications related to this RFI may be submitted electronically to Ms. Liz Bonilla-Sotomayor at liz.c.bonilla-sotomayor.civ@us.navy.mil and Ms. Andrea Longo at andrea.t.longo.civ@us.navy.mil. Verbal questions will not be accepted. Questions shall not contain classified information. Please ensure that the subject line of any emails containing responses or questions related to this notice includes the name of your firm and �Automated Celestial Navigation System (ACNS) RFI Response� (without quotation marks) in the subject line. Responses are limited to a maximum of fifteen (15) pages in length, excluding the cover page, within a minimum font size of 10 points. Generic capability statements that do not address the information requested in this RFI will be deemed non-responsive without any further communication from the Government. All responsive submissions received by the due date noted in this RFI may be considered by the Government to inform the resulting Request for Proposal. All information received bearing proprietary markings will be handled in accordance with applicable statutes and regulations. Responses to this notice will not be returned and will be maintained or destroyed in accordance with the Government�s records management policy. An acknowledgement of receipt will be provided for all responses received. If you do not receive an acknowledgement within two working days, please notify the points of contact listed in this notice. All materials submitted in response to this RFI should be UNCLASSIFIED. Responses to this notice must include the following: Include a cover page containing the following information: Sources Sought number for this notice (N00024-27-RFPREQ-IWS-6-0002) Company Name Mailing address and physical address (if different) DUNS number CAGE code Business size status (based on NAICS code 334511) Type of small business (if applicable) Facility Security Clearance (FSC) level Name, position, email address, and phone number of point(s) of contact Interested parties submitting proposed solutions shall include the following in the RFI submission: Provide System Characteristics: Average position fix accuracy of the proposed system; Operational capabilities across day, twilight, and nighttime conditions; Ephemeris data age for fix accuracy; How quality of each position fix is indicated; Ability of the system to accept data formats sourced from the United States Naval Observatory (USNO); Type of Earth Orientation Parameter (EOP) data format; Average position fix frequency rate (for Stars-Only and Stars-Satellites). Provide Component Characteristics: 1) What is the current configuration of the proposed system? 2) Sensor volume and physical dimensions; 3) Sensor weight; 4) What environmental Military Standards does your proposed system meet (i.e. MIL-STD-810H CH1 (Environmental Engineering Considerations and Laboratory Tests), MIL-STD-167-1A (Mechanical Vibrations of Shipboard Equipment), MIL-DTL-901E (High-Impact Mechanical Shock for Shipboard Machinery and Equipment), and MIL-STD-461H (Electromagnetic Interference Characteristics of Subsystems and Equipment)? title: CPE CBRND Seeking Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) on Aluminum Flakes for Screening Obscuration Module - Multispectral (SOM-M)
description: 1.0 Disclaimer This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the U.S. Government (USG) to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the USG will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this RFI. Responders are advised that the USG will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. The information gathered by this RFI will be shared with relevant interested USG parties to help inform future development and procurement efforts. 2.0 Background The Joint Product Manager for CBRN Layered Effects is responsible for enabling and enhancing the survivability of our Joint Warfighters so they can fight and win across all domains in a CBRN-contested environment. As the acquisition leader in mobile analytics, our portfolio provides transformative solutions � including advanced reconnaissance systems, sensors, and mobile analytical laboratories � that ensure our military is safeguarded against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats. To support this mission, the USG is pursuing the Screening Obscuration Module - Multispectral (SOM-M) program, which is envisioned as a modular, man-portable, ground-emplaced obscuration and screening system designed to produce a multispectral obscurant cloud for both mounted and dismounted use. In support of the SOM-M program, the USG is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify alternative, cost-effective commercial manufacturing options for critical, novel bispectral obscurant material. The technical requirements for this capability are detailed in Section 4.0 of this document. 3.0 Purpose The purpose of this RFI is to survey industry capabilities and identify alternative commercial manufacturing options for a novel bispectral obscurant material. Specifically, the USG seeks to identify manufacturers capable of performing high-volume Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) onto Aluminum Flakes at a commercial scale, and to assess industry readiness to support a potential Army-funded manufacturing maturation project aimed at reducing sustainment costs. 4.0 Technical Requirements Interested parties must demonstrate capabilities or conceptual pathways to meet the following production and material requirements: Base Material & Size: Aluminum Flake sized at 2 � 4 microns. Coating Process & Material: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) onto the aluminum flakes. Target Production Volume: Scalable to large commercial quantities, ranging from hundreds of pounds (lbs) to tons. Cost Efficiency: Proposed alternative manufacturing options must significantly reduce current manufacturing protocol costs to ensure long-term sustainment capability for the military services. 5.0 Requested Information Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI providing a white paper including technical insights on the manufacturing feasibility, cost-effectiveness, and scalability of the proposed Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) process. Ideal responses will include the following elements: Manufacturing/Production Approach: A comprehensive overview of the proposed methodology to achieve the PVD coating of Silicon Dioxide (SiO2) on Aluminum Flakes (2 � 4 microns). This should include details on the facility scale, equipment, and proposed lead times based on the scale of material produced. Cost Projections & Scale: Estimated cost profiles and projected cost-reduction curves when scaling production from hundreds of pounds to tons, demonstrating how the approach achieves a sustainable cost profile for long term acquisition. Maturity, Capacity, & Risks: An assessment of current facility readiness, current and potential production capacity, and identified technical and manufacturing challenges or risk factors associated with scaling this specific PVD coating process. Company Information & Past Performance: A brief summary of relevant company experience, facility capabilities, or prior similar material coating efforts. 6.0 Submission Requirements All submissions must be electronic and adhere to the following formatting and content rules: Page Limit: All responses shall be no longer than five (5) pages. Formatting: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages, with font size no smaller than 10-point. Company Information: Include official company name, address, telephone number, website, and business type (large/small business classification), CAGE Code. title: Germany – Office block construction work – Vergabeverfahren zum Erwerb einer Neuen Zentrale der Deutschen Bundesbank
description: Die Deutsche Bundesbank (nachfolgend auch "Bundesbank" oder "Auftraggeberin" genannt) ist die Zentralbank der Bundesrepublik Deutschland. Sie hat Verfassungsrang als bundesunmittelbare juristische Person des öffentlichen Rechts und ist integraler Bestandteil des Europäischen Systems der Zentralbanken. Sie wirkt mit dem vorrangigen Ziel, die Preisstabilität zu gewährleisten, verwaltet die Währungsreserven, sorgt für die bankmäßige Abwicklung des Zahlungsverkehrs im Inland und Ausland und trägt zur Stabilität der Zahlungs- und Verrechnungssysteme bei. Ihre Zentrale befindet sich in Frankfurt am Main und steht für die Erfüllung dieser gesetzlichen Kernaufgaben sowie die öffentliche Wahrnehmung der Institution. Mit dem Ende der Nutzungsdauer der bisherigen Zentrale und einer interimistischen Unterbringung in angemieteten Flächen ergibt sich für die Bundesbank die Notwendigkeit, eine moderne, repräsentative und zukunftsfähige Liegenschaft für die künftige Zentrale der Bundesbank zu erwerben. Der Erwerb der Liegenschaft auf der Grundlage eines noch zu verhandelnden Grundstückskaufvertrages mit Bauverpflichtung (Bauträgervertrag mit endfälliger Zahlung zum Festpreis) (auch "Kaufvertrag" genannt) ist Gegenstand dieses Vergabeverfahrens. Der Grundstückskaufvertrag bedarf der notariellen Beurkundung. Es ist derzeit vorgesehen, dass die Zuschlagserteilung und die notarielle Beurkundung in unmittelbarem zeitlichen Zusammenhang erfolgen. Der Entwurf des Grundstückskaufvertrages wird den im Teilnahmewettbewerb ausgewählten Bietern von der Bundesbank als Verhandlungsgrundlage zur Verfügung gestellt. Ziel der Beschaffung ist die Bündelung der Arbeitsplätze der Zentrale in einer Liegenschaft und die Abbildung der in den Vergabeunterlagen beschriebenen Anforderungen und Funktionen in einem Ensemble, das architektonisch und funktional den besonderen Anforderungen der Bundesbank entspricht. Nach derzeitigem Stand sind die Anforderungen der Bundesbank in einem zusammenhängenden Gebäudeensemble umzusetzen. Eine Änderung dieser Anforderungen ist im Rahmen des Verhandlungsverfahrens möglich. In der Liegenschaft sind Flächen für verschiedene Sonderfunktionen zu integrieren. Hierzu zählen nach aktuellem Stand beispielsweise ein differenziertes Konferenz- und Besprechungsangebot, eine umfassende Betriebsgastronomie (einschließlich Vorstandsgastronomie), Flächen für Fahrbereitschaft und Logistik sowie Sicherheitszentralen. Es ist nicht ausgeschlossen, dass Sonderfunktionen im Rahmen des Verhandlungsverfahrens entfallen, geändert werden oder andere Sonderfunktionen hinzukommen. Zur Umsetzung der Anforderungen kommt sowohl ein Neubau als auch eine Kernsanierung eines bestehenden Gebäudes oder eine Kombination hieraus in Betracht. Die Abnahme und Übergabe der vertragsgemäß hergestellten Liegenschaft durch die Bundesbank muss nach aktueller Planung spätestens sieben Jahre nach Zuschlagserteilung erfolgen (Meilenstein). Die zeitlichen Vorgaben und die Meilensteine können sich im Laufe des Vergabeverfahrens ändern. Eine verbindliche Festlegung der zeitlichen Vorgaben ist im Laufe des Verhandlungsverfahrens für alle Meilensteine vorgesehen. Nach § 2 S. 2 des Gesetzes über die Deutsche Bundesbank hat die Bundesbank ihren Sitz in Frankfurt am Main. Das Auswahlgebiet, in welchem die verfahrensgegenständliche Liegenschaft liegen muss, ist das Stadtgebiet Frankfurt am Main mit der sicherheitsbedingten Ausnahme der Bereiche des Flughafenareals und der nahegelegenen Gateway Gardens (Gemarkung 0518). Das Auswahlgebiet ergibt sich aus der Unterlage Auswahlgebiet (Anlage 1) und ist bei der Wahl des Standortes zwingend einzuhalten. Bei Widersprüchen hinsichtlich des Auswahlgebietes zwischen der Beschreibung in den übrigen Vergabeunterlagen und Anlage 1 gilt Anlage 1 vorrangig. Werden Grundstücke und/oder Liegenschaften angeboten, die sich ganz oder teilweise außerhalb des Auswahlgebietes befinden, führt dies zum zwingenden Ausschluss des Teilnahmeantrages. Die Liegenschaft muss auf einem Grundstück im Auswahlgebiet hergestellt werden, über welches der Auftragnehmer nach Maßgabe der Vergabeunterlagen im Zuschlagsfall zur Erbringung der ausgeschriebenen Leistung rechtssicher verfügen und der Bundesbank Eigentum an dem zu bebauenden Grundstück frei von nicht übernommenen Belastungen nach Maßgabe der Vergabeunterlagen, insbesondere des Grundstückskaufvertrages und seiner Anlagen verschaffen kann. Der Grundstückskaufvertrag und die Anforderungen an das Grundstück sind Gegenstand der Vertragsverhandlungen in der Verhandlungsphase und können sich noch ändern. Von den Bewerbern bzw. den Bietern sind nach Maßgabe der Vergabeunterlagen Erklärungen zum Grundstück abzugeben, aus denen sich je nach Verfahrensstufe immer konkreter ergibt, ob das angebotene Grundstück die Anforderungen der Bundesbank erfüllt. Welche Unterlagen diesbezüglich mit dem Teilnahmeantrag einzureichen sind, ergibt sich aus der Checkliste der vom Bewerber einzureichenden Unterlagen, die mit den Vergabeunterlagen zur Verfügung gestellt wird. Die Liegenschaft mit der noch zu errichtenden oder umzubauenden Immobilie muss die Anforderungen der Bundesbank erfüllen, die in den Vergabeunterlagen, insbesondere der Funktionalen Leistungsbeschreibung, im Raum- und Funktionsprogramm sowie den jeweils näher definierten Ausstattungs- und Nutzungsvorgaben aufgeführt sind. Diese Unterlagen sind Gegenstand der Vergabeunterlagen, die ausschließlich den Bietern, die zur Abgabe eines Angebotes aufgefordert werden, zur Verfügung gestellt werden. Eine Änderung oder Konkretisierung der Anforderungen im Rahmen des Verhandlungsverfahrens ist möglich. Damit die Bewerber bewerten können, ob sie die Anforderungen - ggf. mit Konsortialpartnern und/oder Nachunternehmern und/oder Eignungsgebern erfüllen können, ist den Vergabeunterlagen zum Teilnahmewettbewerb eine Informative Leistungsbeschreibung beigefügt.
